NDIA-ICT-TEP-001
1. Governance, risk and exceptions
Governance, risk, internal control and exceptions

Technology-enabled projects must operate under approved NDIA governance that assigns accountable owners, manages delivery, security, shared and emerging risks against NDIA risk appetite, maintains internal controls, and records any approved exceptions, compensating controls, expiry dates and escalation decisions.
Applies to all technology-enabled projects, material project changes, shared risks and any requested security exception or compensating control.

2. Investment, assurance and benefits
Portfolio investment, assurance, gate decisions and benefits

Project proposals and gate decisions must align with NDIA corporate, digital investment and portfolio priorities; document options, costs, benefits, dependencies and risks; complete required IOF, DTA, contestability and assurance reviews; and track benefits, conditions and assurance actions through implementation and post-implementation review.
Applies from proposal screening through business case, funding, gate approvals, delivery, transition, closure and post-implementation review.

3. Architecture, reuse and interoperability
Architecture review, reuse, interoperability and integration

Projects must complete architecture review before procurement or build, reuse existing NDIA, Commonwealth or market capabilities where practical, and design new solutions with reusable components, APIs, interoperability, integration standards, supportability and clear operational ownership.
Applies before investment approval, ICT capability development, digital procurement, build approval and major architecture change.

4. Participants, privacy and protected information
Participant-centred legal authority, privacy and protected Agency information

Projects must confirm legal authority and business ownership, assess participant, provider and staff impacts, maintain traceable Scheme business rules and review pathways, and apply privacy-by-design and protected Agency information controls to all personal or NDIS information handling, including supplier handling.
Applies to projects that affect participants, providers, staff, Scheme administration, personal information or protected Agency information.

5. Classification, access and data sharing
Information classification, caveats, external sharing and DATA Scheme controls

Projects must classify information and data holdings, apply required markings, caveats and handling controls, restrict access and external, offshore or international sharing to authorised need-to-know arrangements, and use DATA Scheme data sharing agreements and safeguards only where approved.
Applies where projects create, use, store, process, communicate or share official, sensitive, classified, Agency or Australian Government data.

6. Records, FOI, retention and disposal
Records, FOI readiness, metadata, retention, disposal and decommissioning

Projects must create, store and maintain complete auditable records, metadata, FOI-searchable evidence and decision trails in approved systems, and retain, transfer, decommission or dispose of information and technology assets only under approved records, security and disposal authorities.
Applies to all project records, decisions, artefacts, metadata, datasets, workspaces, assets, decommissioning and closure activities.

7. Secure technology lifecycle and authorisation
Secure-by-design lifecycle, system definition, change control and authorisation

Projects must apply an ISM-aligned secure technology lifecycle by defining system boundaries, security objectives, classifications, owners, authorised technology registers and material change triggers; prohibited or legacy technology must have approved mitigations, and no system may go live or continue after material change until residual risk is assessed and authorised.
Applies to new or changed technology systems, legacy technology, prohibited technology exceptions, material changes and declared or candidate Systems of Government Significance.

8. Cyber controls and resilience baseline
Cyber strategy, Essential Eight, control baseline and vulnerability management

Projects must align to NDIA cyber strategy and implement approved baseline cyber controls, including Essential Eight, protective DNS, vulnerability disclosure and remediation, post-quantum cryptography where applicable, smart-device security standards, threat intelligence integration and documented control exceptions before release.
Applies to all ICT, digital, connected-device, internet-connected and cyber-security-impacting project deliverables, tailored by risk and applicability.

9. Cloud, hosting, gateways and data centres
Cloud, hosting, outsourced ICT, gateways and shared responsibility

Projects using cloud, hosting, outsourced government ICT services, data centres, gateways or Secure Service Edge must obtain current IRAP, HCF and approved procurement-pathway evidence, define shared responsibilities, data sovereignty, security, privacy, records, monitoring, backup, disaster recovery, cost management and exit arrangements before approval and operation.
Applies where projects use cloud, hosting, outsourced government ICT services, certified data centres, gateways, Secure Service Edge or internet/classified digital infrastructure.

10. Procurement, contracts and sourcing
Supplier, procurement, contract and digital sourcing governance

Project procurements and contracts must demonstrate value for money, probity and delegate approval; assess supplier, FOCI and security risks; include enforceable security, privacy, records, subcontractor, transition and exit obligations; and manage supplier performance, contract terms, acceptance and risk reassessments over the contract lifecycle.
Applies to sourcing, procurement planning, market approaches, contracts, contract extensions, supplier-managed delivery, subcontracting, acceptance and transition.

11. Physical security dependencies
Physical security, facilities, security zones and technology asset protection

Projects affecting facilities or housing technology assets must involve protective security early and verify facility plans, site selection, access controls, construction standards, security zone or SCIF certification and accreditation, storage, alarms, guards, visitor controls and TSCM are approved and commensurate with classification, aggregation and business impact before operational use.
Applies where projects affect facilities, physical environments, security zones, classified or high-impact assets, storage, visitor access, outsourced facilities, SCIFs or TOP SECRET systems.
